trust_decision.summary: Decided here: whether a signature was produced while the Fulcio signing certificate was valid, by calling X509Certificate.checkValidity() on the tlog entry's integrated_time, in KeylessVerifier.verify for a bundle; the authenticity of that integrated_time therefore depends on the entry carrying a verified SET (v1) or on a separately verified signing time, and that dependency is not enforced.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names bundle verification of integratedTime, and this is the only place in the verification flow that reads integratedTime and turns it into a certificate-validity decision.

fix_sites.entry_point: KeylessVerifier.verify(byte[]|Path, Bundle, VerificationOptions), reached from the sigstore-cli 'verify' command (sigstore-cli/src/main/java/dev/sigstore/cli/Verify.java:164-168)
RekorVerifier.verifyEntry(RekorEntry) public API, also called from KeylessVerifier.verify (KeylessVerifier.java:180) and KeylessSigner (KeylessSigner.java:410)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: README.md:79 states the public stable API is limited to KeylessSigner and KeylessVerifier and that other classes are subject to change, so a solver can call the RekorEntryFetcher path a compat helper for assembling bundles from detached signing materials rather than a verification entry point, even though it applies the same checkValidity(integratedTime) filter without ever verifying the entry's SET.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Entries with no SET are legitimate: Rekor v2 tlog entries carry no InclusionPromise/SET and establish signing time through separately verified RFC3161 timestamps, and Bundle.checkAtLeastOneTimestamp already accepts a bundle that has only timestamps. A fix that demands a SET on every entry, or that rejects SET-less entries or timestamp-only bundles, breaks these legitimate paths.

O6_input_shapes: tlog entry whose inclusionPromise.signedEntryTimestamp is present (v1/SET, the only shape whose integratedTime is signed via RekorEntry.getSignableContent)
tlog entry whose inclusionPromise is present but signedEntryTimestamp is empty (dropped by BundleReader, treated as SET-less)
tlog entry with no inclusionPromise at all (Rekor v2 shape)
tlog entry whose integrated_time is absent (parses as 0, e.g. the v2 fixture) versus present and attacker-chosen
bundle carrying only rfc3161 timestamps and no SET

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A tlog entry with no SET is accepted by the public RekorVerifier (SET verification is skipped when the string is null/empty), so nothing authenticates its integrated_time even when it comes from a v1 log.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: ProtoMutators.java:84 documents that Rekor v2 entries have no SET, so a solver reads SET absence as an expected, supported shape rather than an unprotected route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package from the landing point (dev.sigstore.rekor.client)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A Bundle assembled through the public builder with an empty-string signedEntryTimestamp satisfies Bundle.checkAtLeastOneTimestamp, which tests only != null, so no RFC3161 timestamp is required even though no SET is verifiable.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: BundleReader only sets a SET when it is non-empty (BundleReader.java:77-83), so the JSON path never produces an empty SET and the gap looks unreachable from a parsed bundle.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package (dev.sigstore.bundle), one file away from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second tlog client path that converts a Rekor v2 TLogEntry response into a RekorEntry, which has no integrated_time field.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This client already exists in-tree but is not wired into KeylessSigner/KeylessVerifier, so a maintainer adding Rekor v2 support would naturally make signer/verifier accept its output.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A save/round-trip path that writes integrated_time from the in-memory RekorEntry, including the 0 value produced for SET-less v2 entries.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: BundleWriter already has a TODO about integrated_time becoming optional (BundleWriter.java:56-58) and special-cases that field, so a maintainer would plausibly add a v2 write branch here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second bundle media-type/legacy reader that populates integrated_time from another source (for example a RekorResponse JSON instead of the bundle proto).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: BundleReader already branches on media type and on certificate vs chain vs public key, so another accepted input dialect is a natural extension point.

O9_family: improper verification of cryptographic signature / signing-time and certificate-validity checks (CWE-347)

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 8.14.1 wrapper (gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties:4), Kotlin DSL with included build-logic builds, JDK toolchain resolved from build parameters (build-logic/basics/src/main/kotlin/configureToolchain.kt:13-24); multi-module (sigstore-java, sigstore-cli, gradle/maven plugins); dependency resolution needs network on first build
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 5 in sigstore-java: KeylessVerifierTest and RekorVerifierTest cover this area, with BundleReaderTest/BundleVerifierTest and the required-field test; fixtures are local (sigstore-java/src/test/resources/dev/sigstore/samples/bundles/*.sigstore and .../rekor-response/valid/entry*.json) and RekorVerifierTest loads a local staging_trusted_root.json, but KeylessVerifierTest constructs the verifier with sigstorePublicDefaults(), which fetches the trusted root over TUF, so those tests need network; the CLI's --trusted-root option (sigstore-cli/src/main/java/dev/sigstore/cli/Verify.java:134-138) shows verification can run offline with a local root.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject any tlog entry without a non-empty SET, which closes the bundle path but breaks legitimate Rekor v2 and RFC3161-timestamp-only bundles instead of establishing an authenticated signing time.
